1Password.com > Developer > Directory > Other (under Infrastructure Secrets Management) > Create a Service Account. A robot's vaults and permissions can never be changed; make a new robot instead. Robots can't reach the built-in Personal, Private, Employee or default Shared vault.

Anyone allowed to create service accounts; if the option is missing, ask an administrator. 8c. What the hub installer does and doesn't do about tunnels (G11)
Does install_hub.sh or rebuild_hub.py create the tunnel?

No. Both need an existing tunnel. Its ID is hard-coded in rebuild_hub.py (TUNNEL_ID), install_hub.sh (TUNNEL_ID) and cf/config.yml (tunnel and credentials-file); its hostname is in cf/config.yml and in the installer's public check. rebuild_hub.py fetches the tunnel's token through Composio and turns it into the credentials file cloudflared reads (AccountTag, TunnelSecret, TunnelID).

Only to manage tunnels (create, route, delete and list them), not to run one. It is account-wide: whoever holds it can create, delete and manage every tunnel in the account. A tunnel runs on its credentials file (locally managed) or its token (remotely managed). The hub holds a cert.pem it doesn't need; G06 lists it as a cleanup.
What may read a tunnel token?
A Write-level tunnel permission: Cloudflare Tunnel Write, Cloudflare One Connectors Write, or Cloudflare One Connector: cloudflared Write. The account token has Edit on every group (G08).
Is the hub's locally-managed tunnel what Cloudflare recommends?

Cloudflare recommends remotely-managed tunnels for most uses and keeps locally-managed ones for specific cases. The installer is built around a locally-managed tunnel; switching would change install_hub.sh and rebuild_hub.py, which is a design change for the Director, not a rebuild step.
